_readme: Where the vendored standards data in this directory came from - PF-007.
This file records provenance, not a verification that did not happen. The environment
PeakFlow is assembled in cannot reach ISO, SWIFT or UNECE, so nothing here was
downloaded. Saying so is the point: a provenance record that implies a fetch and a
checksum against the publisher converts an unknown into a false assurance, and a false
assurance is never re-examined. An honest caveat is re-examined the first time somebody
needs the data to be right.
Each entry therefore states how the file was obtained, what second source it was
cross-checked against inside this process, and what remains unverified. ICU/CLDR ships
with PHP and knows every ISO 4217 and ISO 3166-1 code, so two of these files have a real
independent check. Rec 20 has none, and its entry says so.
sha256 is the digest of the file as reviewed. `bin/verify iso` compares it, so an edit
that nobody recorded is caught at the one place it would be noticed.

cross_checked_with.note: ICU's currency fraction digits come from CLDR, which deliberately differs from ISO 4217 where a subunit has fallen out of use. The divergences are enumerated and frozen in tests/Support/IsoRegistryRules.php; a new one fails the check rather than silently changing what an invoice rounds to.

currencies.tsv.obtained: transcribed from the published code list; not downloaded in this environment
currencies.tsv.cross_checked: every code is known to ICU 74.2 (0 unknown). Exponents are ISO 4217's, NOT ICU's - see cross_checked_with.note
currencies.tsv.unverified: the numeric codes and the exponents were not compared against the publisher's file. The 36 currencies whose exponent is not 2 are each asserted by name in bin/verify, which is where a transcription error in the column that matters would show
currencies.tsv.not_here: names and symbols, which ICU already knows in every locale PeakFlow serves

countries.tsv.obtained: transcribed from the published code list; not downloaded in this environment
countries.tsv.cross_checked: every alpha-2 is a region ICU 74.2 recognises (0 unknown)
countries.tsv.unverified: the alpha-3 and numeric columns. ICU exposes no alpha-3 or numeric mapping through intl, so there is no second source in-process for either
countries.tsv.not_here: country names, which ICU already knows; and whether an IBAN applies, which ISO 13616 answers and Iban::appliesTo() owns

units.tsv.table: Annex I common codes, with Rec 21 extensions where they appear
units.tsv.obtained: transcribed; not downloaded in this environment
units.tsv.cross_checked: nothing. ICU has no Rec 20 mapping, so unlike the two ISO files above this one has no independent source inside the process
units.tsv.unverified: every code. This is the weakest provenance in the directory and the caveat is deliberate: an invoice is validated against the real Rec 20 list by the RECEIVING system, so a wrong code here is rejected there, by a customer's software, with a schema error a salesperson cannot act on
units.tsv.removed: KTM, labelled 'kilometre per hour'. A speed is not a chargeable quantity - a line multiplies a quantity by a unit price, and 3 km/h x 50 SAR is not money - and the label could not be confirmed against the published list from inside this environment. A code whose meaning cannot be sourced has no business validating an e-invoice field
units.tsv.peakflow_additions: the `dimension` column, which is PeakFlow's classification and not part of Rec 20. It exists so that adding three hours to two kilograms can be refused
units.tsv.peakflow_columns: dimension and decimals are both PeakFlow's, not Rec 20's. Rec 20 says what a code means and nothing about precision or compatibility - so a comparison between incompatible units and a quantity with more places than the unit allows are both refused on our classification, and the file says so rather than letting a reader think UNECE published them.
units.tsv.changed: 2026-11-20, PF-247: a `decimals` column was added, per unit. No code, name or dimension was touched - the digest moved because the file gained a column, which is exactly the edit this digest exists to make somebody state out loud rather than slip past.

languages.tsv.table: not a standard registry - this is the product's own list
languages.tsv.obtained: a product decision, not a transcription. ISO 639-1 in full would be 184 languages the product has no translations for, every one offerable in a picker that then renders English
languages.tsv.cross_checked: the plural categories were verified against ICU 74.2 by formatting a six-category ICU message across 0-220 plus fractional and large values and collecting which categories are reachable: ar gives zero,one,two,few,many,other and en gives one,other - exactly the file's contents
languages.tsv.unverified: nothing. Every column either is a product decision or was checked against ICU in-process
languages.tsv.note: `numbering` is the locale's own system (arab for Arabic). It is NOT what a formatter is handed: financial documents in the region conventionally use Western digits even in Arabic text, so the display default is latn and the departure is recorded in config/money.php

iban.tsv.table: per-country IBAN length, with a published registry example per country
iban.tsv.publisher: SWIFT, as the ISO 13616 registration authority
iban.tsv.obtained: transcribed; not downloaded in this environment
iban.tsv.cross_checked: every one of the 80 examples was put through MOD 97-10 before being committed, and all 80 are accepted by the Iban constructor on every bin/verify run. The check digits are a checksum over the whole string, so a validating example is a string that is right to about 1 part in 97 - which makes the example an independent check on the length column: a wrong length would refuse the country's own published IBAN
iban.tsv.unverified: the lengths of the 7 countries with no sourced example (BI, DJ, MN, NI, RU, SD, SO). bin/verify iban counts them and the count may shrink but not grow
iban.tsv.dropped: one candidate example failed MOD 97-10 and was dropped rather than corrected. A corrected example is no longer a registry vector, it is a computed one, and a computed one cannot confirm a length
iban.tsv.not_here: the BBAN structure per country. A structure table taken from memory would refuse real bank accounts, and refusing a customer's genuine IBAN stops them being paid, where accepting a structurally odd one that passes MOD 97-10 costs a rejected payment message with a reason. Deferred to Phase 06, against the registry file itself
